source.title: RATT: Leveraging Unlabeled Data to Guarantee Generalization
source.authors: S. Garg; Sivaraman Balakrishnan; J. Kolter; Zachary Chase Lipton

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including supplementary material, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper trains models on clean data augmented with randomly labeled inputs and reports training behavior on the mislabeled data. It uses this as part of its generalization-bound method, rather than reproducing the original random-label experiment.
record.gate_note: The paper’s primary bound and Table 1 accuracy values do not measure fitting random labels, so they are not rows. The rows below cover only reported outcomes on training with randomly labeled data; cited prior work on early learning is not counted.
record.test_reason: Although developed to obtain generalization bounds, the study reports its own random-label fitting results, confirms clean-before-noisy learning, and examines regularization. Its training sets mix clean examples with a randomly labeled subset.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly right but understates the main contribution: RATT obtains post-training generalization bounds from clean and randomly labeled training errors. The authors prove results for ERM and linear gradient descent under stated conditions, extend to practical deep networks under an additional assumption, empirically confirm early learning, and show that regularization can preserve useful bounds by avoiding interpolation.
record.recipe_differences: The study adds randomly labeled examples to clean data and tracks their fit to construct generalization bounds; it does not reproduce the original whole-training-set random-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: In the wide binary-MNIST experiment, the outcome differs with early stopping or weight decay: without either, training fit is perfect and unseen clean performance is hurt; with either, the clean-performance difference is close to zero. In the deep-network experiments, fit on mislabeled data increases during training and reaches perfect overfitting in the interpolation regime.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding randomly labeled examples has little effect on clean performance under early stopping or weight decay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regularization can preserve clean generalization when training includes an additional randomly labeled subset.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 139, 2021
record.problems: The deep-network extension relies on an assumption about overfitting to the random mixture. Reported random-label fitting outcomes are qualitative, with no separate random-subset training-error values or random-label test errors. Some results are aggregated over 3 seeds without stated error bars.
record.rows_left_out: No rows for bound estimates, clean test-accuracy values, or cited early-learning results: they do not themselves report an outcome on fitting the randomly labeled training data. Figure-only curves were not used to infer precise values.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling of the entire training set and chance-level test error; experiments instead mix clean and randomly labeled examples.
Relative training time for true versus random labels and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
Perfect training fit and steadily increasing test error over a corruption sweep from zero to fully random labels.
Controlled dropout and augmentation comparisons, fully random training sets, and generalization on true labels after removing regularization.

missing.what: The authors' own confirmation of clean-before-mislabeled learning, including the early training condition and subsequent noisy-label fitting. The record incorrectly treats this solely as cited prior work.
missing.locator: Introduction; Section 5, Deep Nets; Section 6, Implicit bias in deep learning

missing.what: Separate fitting outcomes for weight decay and early stopping. The discussion explicitly states that these prevent perfect training fit, and the introduction describes weight decay combined with large initial learning rates avoiding mislabeled-data interpolation while maintaining clean fit. Record conditions separately rather than inferring fitting from clean accuracy.
missing.locator: Introduction; Section 5, Wide Nets; Section 6, Generalization bounds; Appendix C.4

record.verdict_notes: This is not an original source for any version. Unmeasured components do not justify limits_scope verdicts. Early stopping alone is outside V5's named explicit regularizers. No precise curve values or individual-model interpolation endpoints can be recovered from the supplied figure text.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report test error on a test set with random labels or establish that it is at chance. The random labels are assigned to added unlabeled data, not to the entire training set.
No comparison of training time for true versus random labels or sweep over the fraction of corrupted labels.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment.
Varies the amount of added randomly labeled data in some experiments, but does not sweep the fraction of corrupted labels in the training set and report training and test error as specified.

Tests early stopping and weight decay in a wide-network setting, but not dropout or data augmentation as ways to stop random-label fitting. Does not establish that removing regularization alone makes true-label generalization poor across the claimed standard networks.
The paper cites early-learning research and discusses the phenomenon, but its own experiments do not measure whether real labels are learned before random labels.

rows.subject: 2-layer wide network on binary MNIST
rows.size_stated: 200000 hidden units in the described 2-layer wide MLP; width for the reported run not separately stated
rows.operation_detail: Trained with SGD on MSE loss on clean data augmented with randomly labeled data, without early stopping or weight decay.
rows.measure: Training-data fit and unseen clean performance, described qualitatively
rows.value: The training data are perfectly fit; adding extra randomly labeled data hurts unseen clean performance.
rows.uncertainty: Results aggregated over 3 seeds (Figure 2(b)); no error bars stated.
rows.note: The paper says the bound becomes vacuous due to perfect training fit. It does not separately report random-subset training error or test error on random labels.
rows.check: Perfect training fit supports memorization in the mixed-label setting. Poorer clean performance after adding noise does not challenge V5's claim about removing regularization on true-label data. Figure 2(b) varies the added-data fraction; 20% is not its only condition.

rows.note: The statement covers the four named models collectively; the text does not give separate fit values by model. The paper says early stopping produces close test-performance bounds, not that test error on random labels is at chance.
